sections.html:
A cash buyer will usually close a Springettsbury house faster than any other route. The township lies east and northeast of the city of York, and the steps that set the calendar are tax certification, payoff letters and title work.

The township is home to the York Galleria mall and a large Harley-Davidson manufacturing campus. It includes East York, Pleasureville, Yorklyn and Stonybrook, and the housing mixes 1930s homes in East York with postwar subdivisions such as Fayfield and Haines Acres and newer developments.

There are 10,202 households, 72.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $243,900. Median rent is $1,339 and median household income is $86,335. About 85.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and more than a quarter of homes are rented, so some sellers are landlords with tenants to consider.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in
sections.html:
Springettsbury is split between the York Suburban and Central York school districts, and your tax bills follow whichever one serves your address. The township tax collector bills school real estate tax for both districts inside the township.

Why it matters: the split changes your sale paperwork. School tax is billed separately from the county and township bill, on a different date, and a closing company needs the right district and the right year to prorate it correctly. Pull your latest school tax bill, since it names the district, and keep it beside the parcel number for the title company.

Springettsbury tax calendar and fees
Tax itemDate or fee
County and municipal tax bills mailedFebruary 15
York Suburban school tax bills mailedJuly 1
Central York school tax bills mailedJuly 15
Real estate tax certification for a sale$20, check to the Tax Collector
Prior year delinquent taxYork County Tax Claim Bureau, 717-771-9232

The collector goes by postmark date for mailed payments, so allow time. Cash is not accepted in the drop box. If your mortgage company pays through escrow, forward any bill that reaches you rather than paying twice.

Your closing company requests a Real Estate Tax Certification from the township Tax Collector. It shows whether York County, township, street light and school taxes are paid, with the year, face amount, discount and penalty for each. The request form carries the property address, parcel number, owner, buyer and settlement date and says whether the deal is a sale or a refinance.

The fee is $20, payable by check to the Springettsbury Township Tax Collector. Delinquent taxes from prior years go through the York County Tax Claim Bureau instead. A sewer account certification request form also exists, so ask the title company whether a sewer certification is on its list.

Springettsbury employs a full-time Codes Enforcement Officer who responds to complaints about property maintenance. The issues that come up most often are:

  • Fences, pools, decks, sheds and patios built too close to a property line.
  • Signs of the wrong size, type or location.
  • Cars, RVs, tractors, construction equipment and boats parked on grass, plus abandoned or junk vehicles.
  • Weeds, tall grass, trash, uncleared sidewalks, dilapidated buildings and unsafe structures.

Owners are asked to correct a violation voluntarily, and a finding can sometimes be appealed to the Zoning Hearing Board. If a violation stays open, the township can pursue legal action and the District Magistrate can impose fines for each violation. Fix open notices before listing, or tell a cash buyer about them up front so the price reflects the work.

Pennsylvania takes 1 percent of the value as realty transfer tax, and local governments may add their own share. The York County Recorder of Deeds gathers the whole amount when the deed is recorded. Some family transfers and property passed by will or intestate succession are exempt.

Before you estimate your net, ask the Recorder for the combined Springettsbury rate and the recording fees. The sales agreement names who pays, but if the tax goes unpaid both sides answer for it.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale the right choice?
sections.html:
Cash fits best when the house needs work, carries an open code notice, has a tenant on the way out, or must close by a fixed day. Collect a written cash offer, then set it beside what a listing would net once commission, repair credits and months of carrying costs are taken out.

Ask any buyer who covers the tax certification fee, the sewer certification and the recording costs, and ask for the closing date in writing.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or an inherited house
sections.html:
A house with a tenant leaving, or one passing through an estate, adds a few questions. Check the lease end date first and plan the closing day around it. If a family member inherited the property, ask the Recorder of Deeds or the title company whether an exemption applies to your deed, because transfers by will or intestate succession can be exempt from the state tax.

Whoever signs the deed needs clear legal authority, and the title company will want to see it before it books settlement. Gather the deed, the school tax bill that names the district, and any township notices into one folder. A cash buyer usually moves faster when those papers are ready on day one, and you avoid last-week surprises over who pays a certification fee or a recording cost.

If open code notices exist, decide whether you will correct them or sell as-is with the price adjusted. Telling the buyer early is better than having a lender or an inspector raise it later.

1. Find the district on your latest school tax bill and keep the bill with the parcel number.
  2. Check your address for open code notices or permit questions by calling the township office, and fix what you can before listing.
  3. Ask the closing company to send the tax certification request form with the settlement date, and have a $20 check payable to the Tax Collector ready.
  4. Pay any prior-year delinquent tax through the York County Tax Claim Bureau, and ask the title company whether a sewer certification is needed.
  5. Get the combined local transfer tax rate and recording fees from the York County Recorder of Deeds, and settle in the contract who pays.
  6. If you are a landlord, check lease dates before you agree to a closing day.

A cash buyer can skip the lender and appraisal wait, which leaves these items as the true schedule. Collect them first and the closing date stops depending on guesswork.

faqs.q: Does Springettsbury Township require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Call the township office to ask about open violations or permits on your address before listing. The code officer responds to complaints and permits, so clear any open notices first.

faqs.q: How much is the tax certification in Springettsbury?
faqs.a: The fee is $20, paid by check to the Springettsbury Township Tax Collector. The closing company sends the request form with the parcel number, owner, buyer and settlement date.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Springettsbury Township?
faqs.a: York Suburban and Central York both serve parts of the township. Their tax bills go out July 1 for York Suburban and July 15 for Central York.

faqs.q: When are Springettsbury county and township tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: County and municipal bills are mailed February 15. School bills are separate, and the collector goes by postmark date for mailed payments.

faqs.q: Where do I pay back taxes on a Springettsbury house?
faqs.a: Delinquent taxes from prior years go to the York County Tax Claim Bureau at 717-771-9232. Current-year bills are paid to the township Tax Collector, who goes by postmark date.
